Harpreet Singh Brar, J. (Oral)

This petition has been filed under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 seeking
anticipatory bail in case bearing Fir No.332 dated 07.11.2023 (Annexure P-1) under Sections
406/420 of Ipc registered at Police Station Kalka, District Panchkula.
On 11.02.2025, the following order was passed:-

'Instant petition is preferred under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha
Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'Bnss') seeking anticipatory bail in Fir No.332 dated
07.11.2023 under Sections 406 & 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, registered at
Police Station Kalka, District Panchkula.

Learned counsel for the petitioner, inter alia, contends that FIR (supra) was registered after 07 years from the purchase of the property and after more than 02 years and 11 months from the date of filing of civil suit.
The status quo is already in favour of the complainant.

The dispute is purely civil in nature, which has been given Bakshind Kaur Alias Bakshinder Kaur vs State Of Haryana on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124790975/
1 the criminal colour.

sentences.text: The petitioner is 74 years old widow, who is suffering from various age related ailments.

Moreover, the maximum sentence provided for the o f f e n c e s , u n d e r w h i c h t h e F I R ( s u p r a ) i s 1 o f 3 N e u t r a l C i t a t i o n No:=2025:PHHC:034364 registered, is punishable upto 07 years
and no notice under Section 35(3) of BNSS [erstwhile Section 41-A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.')] has been served upon the petitioner.
Notice of motion.

Ms. Geeta Sharma, DAG, Haryana, who is present in the Court, accepts notice on behalf of the respondent-State and Mr. Ajay Sharma, Advocate accepts notice on behalf of the complainant and files his Vakalatnama in the Court today, which is taken on record.
Registry is directed to tag the same at the appropriate place of the case file.

Learned counsel for the complainant opposes the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioner on the ground that FIR (supra) was registered after conducting a detailed enquiry by the jurisdictional police authorities and fraud played by the petitioner came to knowledge of the complainant in the month of December, 2022.
Adjourned to 11.03.2025.

Keeping in view the ratio of law enunciated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Arnesh Kumar Vs.
State of Bihar, (2014) 8 SCC 273, Arnab Manoranjan Goswami Vs. State of Maharashtra, (2021) 2 SCC 427, Satender Kumar Antil Vs. CBI, (2022) 10 SCC 51, Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre Vs. State of Maharashtra and ors., 2010 SCC OnLine SC 1375 and Shri Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia Vs. State of Punjab, (1980) 2 SCC 565, the petitioner is directed to appear before Investigating Officer within a period of two weeks from today and thereafter, as directed by the Investigating Officer.

Nothing observed hereinabove shall be construed as an 2 of 3 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:034364 expression of opinion by this Court and learned trial Court shall decide the case on its own merits, strictly in accordance with law.'

In view of the statement of learned State counsel, order dated 11.02.2025 is hereby made absolute.

opennyai_summary.decision:
In the event of arrest, the petitioner will be admitted to interim anticipatory bail on furnishing bail/surety bonds to the satisfaction of Investigating/Arresting Officer.
The petitioner shall cooperate with the investigation/Arresting Officer and abide by the conditions as provided under Section 482(2) of BNSS (erstwhile Section 438(2) of Cr.P.C.).
If the Arresting Officer does not permit the petitioner to join the investigation, he would appear before learned Illaqa Magistrate, who would then summon the Arresting Officer and direct him to join the petitioner in the investigation, in terms of the order of this Court.
In view of the statement of learned State counsel, order dated 11.02.2025 is hereby made absolute.
